Consult Summary:
- Adult with acute asthma-like symptoms (wheeze, cough, shortness of breath) for 2–3 days, now with ongoing symptoms despite blue inhaler use; plan includes GP evaluation in next few days, interim inhaled therapy up-titration, red-flag guidance, and possible antibiotics/steroids depending on exam findings.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Wheezing, coughing, and shortness of breath beginning about 2–3 days ago, triggered by running; able to talk during run previously but now short of breath with exertion; used blue (salbutamol) inhaler with little relief.
- Symptom timeline: Symptoms started 2–3 days ago and have persisted; previously well controlled until the last 2–3 days.
- Severity/impact: Shortness of breath on brisk walking and running; wheeze and cough present; no sputum reported.
- Exacerbating factors: Exertion (running/brisk walking).
- Relieving factors: Inhalers used; however, blue inhaler provided limited relief.
- Respiratory history: Asthma diagnosed in the past; last asthma attack 3–4 years ago; no oral steroids or antibiotics in the past (per patient recall).
- Past treatment/maintenance: Using brown inhaler (Clenil) as preventive; using blue inhaler as needed; currently using brown inhaler twice daily (3 puffs previously) with plan to increase to 4 puffs twice daily; blue inhaler use increases during symptoms (every 2–4 hours per clinician guidance; some inconsistency in exact frequency discussed).
- Peak flow: Baseline peak flow reported around 380 (patient’s normal/over time); no peak flow measurement performed during current symptoms.
- Allergies: Hay fever (allergic rhinitis); no medication allergies reported.
- Other meds currently used (documented in conversation): Salbutamol inhaler (blue); Clenil (inhaled corticosteroid, brown); Hydrocortisone (topical); Cetraben (emollient); Bactroban (topical antibiotic) noted by patient; exact doses/frequencies not consistently documented in transcript.
- Personal/social: Not documented in transcript regarding smoking, alcohol, or substance use.
- Family history: Brother with asthma; sister with eczema.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (history with last attack 3–4 years ago; last review ~2 years ago; previously well controlled until recent days).
- Eczema (history; current topical hydrocortisone and emollients).
- Hay fever / allergic rhinitis.

Social History:
- Not documented beyond what is provided above (no smoking/alcohol/substance use details).

Family History:
- Brother with asthma.
- Sister with eczema.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Examination findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- Peak expiratory flow: Baseline reported ~380 (patient’s normal); no current peak flow measurement performed during symptoms.
- Chest exam: Planned during in-person assessment; results not provided in transcript.
- Additional investigations: Not documented; clinician noted possible need for antibiotics and steroids depending on examination.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation (exacerbation on background of otherwise controlled asthma)
- Assessment: Small to moderate exacerbation suspected given new/worsening dyspnea with exertion, wheeze, and inadequate relief from blue inhaler.
- Plan:
  - GP evaluation: Arrange/advise a GP (or nurse-led asthma review) in next few days.
  - Interim inhaled therapy:
    - Increase brown inhaler (Clenil) dose from current to 4 puffs twice daily.
    - Salbutamol (blue inhaler) up to every 2 hours as needed; earlier guidance mentioned up to every 2–4 hours; advised to seek care if used frequently (indicates poor control).
  - Red flags: If breathing worsens, go to A&E immediately.
  - Investigations during interim visit: Chest examination and peak flow measurement; results will guide further management.
  - Possible treatments based on exam: May require antibiotics and systemic steroids if indicated by assessment.
  - Follow-up: Call support and arrange an in-person assessment; physician will recommend face-to-face review.

Issue 2: Eczema (atopic dermatitis) management
- Assessment: History of eczema; currently using topical hydrocortisone and emollients.
- Plan:
  - Continue current topical regimens (hydrocortisone and Cetraben/emollients) as previously prescribed.

Issue 3: Allergic rhinitis / hay fever
- Assessment: Hay fever reported; no specific active management changes discussed.
- Plan:
  - No new therapies documented in the transcript; may consider future allergen management if clinically indicated.

General plan items:
- Continue to monitor symptoms; use rescue inhaler as advised.
- If symptoms worsen or fail to improve with the up-titrated regimen, seek urgent care or A&E.
- Ensure follow-up with GP for asthma review within the next few days.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (BP, pulse, resp rate, temp, oxygen saturation) not provided.
  - Comprehensive medication reconciliation (exact doses, routes, and frequencies for all inhaled therapies; the transcript provides some dosing clues but not precise, consistent values).
  - Smoking status, alcohol/substance use status not documented.
  - Immunization status not documented.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Inhaler frequency for salbutamol is described inconsistently (every 2–4 hours initially, then “every two hourly” in subsequent guidance).
- Transcript quality:
  - Some transcription ambiguities and brand/medication spellings (e.g., “Flanel Bactroban,” “Cetraben,” “Clenil”) and minor phrasing inconsistency; overall, clinically usable with noted ambiguities.
